title: Keto Strawberry Cheesecake Cupcakes
description: These cupcakes taste like strawberry cheesecake in a small, easy to eat form. I swirl fresh strawberry puree right into the almond flour batter before baking, so every bite has real fruit flavor. The frosting is a whipped cream cheese mix, light and tangy, not heavy or sweet. I tested this recipe three times in my own kitchen to get the crumb right. Almond and coconut flour need extra egg and cream cheese to stay moist, so this batter has both. The result is a soft, tender cupcake that holds its shape. This is a great pick for anyone on a low carb or keto plan who still wants a treat that feels special. It also works well for spring parties or berry season baking.

metaDescription: Try this keto strawberry cheesecake cupcakes recipe with fresh berry swirl and whipped frosting. Low carb, easy to bake at home. Get the full recipe now.
ingredients: 8 oz cream cheese, softened, for frosting
1 cup heavy cream, cold, for frosting
12 small fresh strawberry slices, for garnish
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F. Line a muffin pan with 12 paper liners.
Puree the fresh strawberries in a small blender until smooth. Set aside.
Whisk almond flour, coconut flour, erythritol, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
In a separate bowl, beat 4 oz cream cheese with melted butter until smooth.
Add eggs, heavy cream, and vanilla to the cream cheese mix. Beat until combined.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Stir just until no dry flour remains.
Divide batter evenly among the liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Drop small spoonfuls of strawberry puree on top of each cupcake. Swirl gently with a toothpick.
Bake for 16 to 18 minutes, until the tops spring back when touched lightly.
Cool cupcakes in the pan for 10 minutes, then move to a wire rack to cool fully.
For frosting, beat 8 oz cream cheese with powdered erythritol and vanilla until smooth.
In a cold bowl, whip the heavy cream to stiff peaks, then fold into the cream cheese mix.
Pipe frosting onto fully cooled cupcakes. Top each with a fresh strawberry slice.
tips: Pat the strawberry puree dry with a spoon before swirling if it looks watery, so the batter does not turn soggy.
Chill the frosting bowl and beaters for 10 minutes before whipping the cream. This helps it hold stiff peaks.
Do not overmix the batter once the dry and wet ingredients meet. Almond flour batters can turn dense fast.
Store leftovers in the fridge, since the cream cheese frosting is soft and needs to stay cold.
conclusion: These cupcakes bring real strawberry flavor and cheesecake tang to a keto dessert plate. Once you get the swirl technique down, this recipe becomes an easy go-to for warm weather baking.

faq.question: Why did my strawberry swirl sink into the batter?
faq.answer: This happens if the puree is too thin or the batter is too warm. Use ripe, firm strawberries and swirl gently on top, not deep into the batter.

faq.question: Can I use frozen strawberries for the puree?
faq.answer: Yes, but thaw them fully and drain the extra liquid first. Wet puree can make the cupcakes gummy in the center.

faq.question: How many net carbs are in one cupcake?
faq.answer: Each cupcake has about 4 grams net carbs, based on 6 grams total carbs minus 2 grams fiber. This can shift slightly with your exact brand of sweetener.

faq.question: Can I make these ahead of time for a party?
faq.answer: Bake the cupcakes up to two days ahead and store them unfrosted in the fridge. Whip and pipe the frosting the same day you serve them for the best texture.
